brief.headline: Update Claude Code tonight: Sonnet 5.5 is now the default
brief.summary:
Claude Code 2.1.284 landed with Sonnet 5.5 as the API default (same price as Sonnet 5, 30%+ faster, up to 30% cheaper), a new "Yes, but ask again next time" auto-mode answer that cuts repeat permission prompts, and live dollar spend in /usage and the status line so a runaway overnight run gets caught before morning. Update and switch your subagent config to Sonnet 5.5 now; it's a straight win with no tradeoff.

On top of that, two skills claim to make agents check their own work before handing you a PR: autoprompt (45% fewer failures, claimed) and fable-method's think/act/prove eval — both worth a one-ticket test tonight rather than a blind adopt. For spend, codex-chatgpt-web and codex-with-chatgpt let you route Codex work through an existing ChatGPT Pro session instead of metered quota, and kimi-k3-in-c runs a trillion-parameter-class model's inference on a spare CPU in 8GB RAM for zero-cost background tasks. And a real failure report is worth more caution than any of the launches: an unattended agent auto-replied "Yep I'm here!" on someone's behalf, asserting a state it couldn't verify, and cost them a pickup and a rating — check your own hooks for the same pattern before you extend an agent's leash further.
bullets: Update Claude Code to 2.1.284, confirm Sonnet 5.5 default, pick "Yes, but ask again next time" to cut auto-mode interruptions
Watch dollar spend live in /usage and the status line to catch a runaway overnight run before morning
A/B the autoprompt skill (claimed 45% fewer failures) and fable-method's think/act/prove eval on one real ticket tonight
Route Codex through a ChatGPT Pro web session via codex-chatgpt-web, or plan with ChatGPT and execute with Codex via codex-with-chatgpt, to spare API quota
Run Kimi K3 locally in 8GB RAM with kimi-k3-in-c for zero-marginal-cost background agent work
Audit any auto-reply or status-confirming hook for unverifiable claims after the Muse AI Agent "Yep I'm here" incident cost someone a pickup

signals.label: Cost per agent-turn
signals.note: Sonnet 5.5 cuts cost 30% at the same sticker price, ChatGPT-as-backend tools route around metered API quota, and a trillion-parameter model now runs on a spare CPU in 8GB RAM

signals.label: Self-verifying agent runs
signals.note: Multiple new skills (autoprompt, fable-method) and harnesses (dscode auto-approval, ACRYL persistent context) target longer unattended runs with fewer stalls, but claims are self-reported and untested by the reader

signals.label: Verified failure evidence
signals.note: Only one concrete unattended-agent failure account this cycle (Muse AI Agent's false presence claim) against a wave of unverified capability claims from new tools

signals.label: Harness and control-plane options
signals.note: HarnessRouter, zeron, FrontierAgent and deepseek-harness are all shipping competing unified layers for driving Claude Code/Codex/Cursor, none yet consolidated

items.title: Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill — Autoprompt is a coding-agent skill that cuts failures by 45% on agentic coding tasks.
items.tldr: Autoprompt, a coding-agent skill, claims a 45% cut in failures on agentic coding tasks.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in skill that could mean fewer overnight runs that stall or go off-track, if the claim holds on your own repo.
items.tryThis: Install the autoprompt skill and A/B it against your current prompt structure on one real ticket tonight.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.284 makes Claude Sonnet 5.5 the API default (1M context, $2/$10 per Mtok, $0.20/Mtok cache reads), adds a "Yes, but ask again next time" auto-mode answer, and shows dollar spend in /usage and the status line.
items.whyItMatters: A cheaper long-context default plus fewer repeat permission prompts push overnight unattended runs closer to reality, and live dollar tracking catches runaway spend before morning.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code, confirm claude-sonnet-5-5 is your default, and pick "Yes, but ask again next time" on the next auto-mode prompt to cut interruptions on long runs.

items.title: miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web — Use ChatGPT Web (including Pro) as a native model in Codex — with context, tools, streaming and images, without using Codex quota.
items.tldr: codex-chatgpt-web lets Codex use a ChatGPT Web session, including Pro, as its model backend with tools, streaming and images, without consuming Codex API quota.
items.whyItMatters: Routes coding-agent work through an existing ChatGPT Pro subscription instead of metered API tokens, a direct way to cut spend.
items.tryThis: Clone miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web and wire it in as a Codex backend to offload work from paid API quota.

items.title: google/artemis — ARTEMIS turns natural-language instructions into reliable Android automation. It automates end-to-end workflows, captures logs, and integrates seamlessly with AI coding assistants such as Antigravity, Codex, and Claude Code
items.tldr: Google's ARTEMIS turns natural-language instructions into end-to-end Android automation, with hooks for Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity.
items.whyItMatters: A solo mobile shipper gets a way to script and verify Android UI flows without hand-writing instrumentation tests.
items.tryThis: Clone google/artemis and wire it into Claude Code to automate one Android test flow tonight.

items.title: trailhq/Graft — Turbocharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini & every coding agent: faster, cheaper, with contextual understanding specific to your codebase.
items.tldr: Graft indexes a codebase into a graph so Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini answer "where is X" from exact file:line lookups.
items.whyItMatters: Cheaper context retrieval means fewer tokens burned per turn, so an agent can run longer before it hits a limit.
items.tryThis: Install Graft in your repo and run `graft map` to compare it against your current grep-based workflow.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model's inference on a single CPU in 8.24GB of RAM using portable C99, no BLAS or GPU needed.
items.whyItMatters: A trillion-parameter-class model now fits on hardware you likely already own, giving you a zero-marginal-cost option for background or exploratory agent work.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and run it on a spare machine with 8GB+ RAM for cost-free background tasks.

items.title: totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids — Cross-platform local MCP capabilities for ChatGPT with Chrome integration, Goal, Compact & Resume, and durable multi-agent workflows.
items.tldr: chat-on-steroids adds local MCP tools, Chrome integration, and a Goal/Compact/Resume cycle for durable multi-agent workflows in ChatGPT.
items.whyItMatters: Compact-and-resume is what keeps a long agent task alive across context limits, directly useful for overnight runs.
items.tryThis: Clone chat-on-steroids and test its Compact & Resume cycle on a task that currently blows your context window.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: Fuxi is a terminal-based AI coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across multiple LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a concrete lever for sending cheaper subtasks to lower-cost models instead of paying full API rates on every call.
items.tryThis: Clone fuxicodex/Fuxi and configure its provider-routing rules to send low-stakes subtasks to a cheaper model.

items.title: HarnessRouter/harnessrouter — HarnessRouter Community Edition: the self-hosted, Apache-2.0 edition of the unified interface for agent harnesses. Run Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, DSH, and more through one API, with sessions, streaming, fi
items.tldr: HarnessRouter Community Edition self-hosts one API for Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, and DSH agent harnesses, under Apache-2.0.
items.whyItMatters: One API standardizes sessions, streaming, and failure handling across the harnesses you already run, on your own infrastructure.
items.tryThis: Clone HarnessRouter and route your Claude Code and Codex sessions through its unified API.

items.title: zeronsh/zeron — A native control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin and other coding agents.
items.tldr: zeron is a native Rust control plane for driving Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Devin from one place.
items.whyItMatters: A control plane is the building block for triggering and checking agent sessions remotely instead of babysitting a terminal.
items.tryThis: Clone zeronsh/zeron and connect it to an existing Claude Code session to test remote control.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills a "think / act / prove" workflow into portable skills with a built-in eval, so a model checks its own output.
items.whyItMatters: A packaged verify-your-own-work skill is exactly what turns an overnight agent run into a reviewable PR.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method, add its skills to Claude Code, and run the eval on your next task.

items.title: qiz029/dscode — A DeepSeek coding agent harness: persistent shell, Ultra subagents, auto approval, Chrome MCP and session telemetry
items.tldr: dscode is a DeepSeek coding agent harness with a persistent shell, subagents, auto-approval, Chrome MCP, and session telemetry.
items.whyItMatters: Auto-approval plus a persistent shell are the exact settings that keep an agent working overnight without stopping for confirmation.
items.tryThis: Clone dscode and test its auto-approval mode on a throwaway branch to see how long it runs unattended.

items.title: acryldev/acryl — ACRYL - Agent Context Relay Yielding Lifecycles. One persistent workspace, one canonical context, any coding agent.
items.tldr: ACRYL gives coding agents one persistent workspace and canonical context that carries across sessions and across different agent tools.
items.whyItMatters: Targets the exact problem of context loss between worktrees, subagents, or overnight session restarts.
items.tryThis: Point ACRYL's workspace at one of your worktrees and check whether context survives a Claude Code session restart.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.tldr: Anthropic ships Claude Sonnet 5.5, priced the same as Sonnet 5 but 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper to run.
items.whyItMatters: He can switch his Claude Code default and subagent model to Sonnet 5.5 now for a straight speed and cost win at no price increase.
items.tryThis: Point your Claude Code default and subagent model config at Sonnet 5.5 today.

items.title: Quoting Muse AI Agent
items.tldr: An unattended agent auto-replied "Yep I'm here!" on someone's behalf while they were away, causing a missed pickup and a bad rating.
items.whyItMatters: It is a concrete unattended-agent failure: an agent asserted unverifiable state as fact, which is exactly the risk in letting an agent act for you while you sleep.
items.tryThis: Audit any auto-reply or status-confirming hook your agents run, and block claims of your presence or state that the agent cannot verify.

items.title: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.
items.tldr: DeepSeek's deepseek-harness, an open-source coding agent harness built around a plugin architecture, has crossed 238,000 GitHub stars.
items.whyItMatters: A fast-growing open harness is a real alternative or supplement to your Claude Code hooks/subagents setup and worth a look before you invest deeper in one stack.
items.tryThis: Clone deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness and compare its plugin API to your current hooks and subagent setup.

items.title: XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt — ChatGPT thinks. Codex works. Use ChatGPT as the planning brain while keeping the Codex harness.
items.tldr: codex-with-chatgpt routes planning to ChatGPT while execution stays on the Codex harness.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete model-tiering pattern: a cheap planning model paired with the execution harness you already trust for code changes.
items.tryThis: Clone codex-with-chatgpt and try it on one feature branch to see if planning quality beats Codex alone.

items.title: ApodexAI/FrontierAgent — 🧩 FrontierAgent, our agent framework, open-sourced alongside it — native command-line TUI, ReAct and Agent Team modes, one command on macOS and Linux, no preinstall, no hard Docker dependency.
items.tldr: FrontierAgent ships as an open-source CLI agent framework with ReAct and Agent Team modes, installing in one command on macOS and Linux with no Docker dependency.
items.whyItMatters: A Docker-free alternative harness for multi-agent coding runs, worth a head-to-head test against your current Claude Code worktree setup.
items.tryThis: Run the one-command install and try Agent Team mode on one real ticket, then compare to your current harness.

items.title: lexmount/moli — Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
items.tldr: moli is a lightweight, fast headless browser written in Rust, built specifically for AI agents to drive.
items.whyItMatters: A lighter alternative to Playwright/Puppeteer for an agent that needs to open a browser to verify a PR's UI before handing it back.
items.tryThis: Swap your agent's headless-browser step to lexmount/moli and benchmark it against your current verification setup.

items.title: Alexwtlf/agentic-product-demo — Create polished product demo videos with AI coding agents and Remotion. The UI is code, not a screen recording.
items.tldr: A GitHub repo, agentic-product-demo, builds polished product demo videos from code using AI coding agents and Remotion instead of screen recordings.
items.whyItMatters: He could adapt this to auto-generate a demo of what an overnight agent run built, cutting time spent reviewing PRs cold in the morning.
items.tryThis: Clone Alexwtlf/agentic-product-demo and wire it into your overnight pipeline to auto-generate a demo video for morning PR review.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.284
items.tldr: Claude Code v2.1.284 ships 100 changes: 12 additions, 13 improvements, 53 fixes, and 10 behavior changes.
items.whyItMatters: Fifty-three fixes in your primary agent harness justify an update, though the digest gives no specifics on what changed.
items.tryThis: Update to Claude Code v2.1.284 and scan the changelog for anything touching hooks or permissions before an overnight run.

clusters.title: Claude Code 2.1.284 makes Sonnet 5.5 the default
clusters.summary: The changelog release, the model announcement, and the version-summary post all describe the same ship: Sonnet 5.5 as API default at Sonnet 5 pricing but faster and cheaper, bundled with auto-mode and spend-tracking changes in Claude Code 2.1.284.

clusters.title: ChatGPT subscription as a free Codex backend
clusters.summary: Two separate repos both wire an existing ChatGPT session into the Codex harness — one as the execution model, one as the planning layer — so coding-agent work bypasses metered API quota.
